bullets.title: BIS Chip Export Controls Freeze Billions in AI Data-Center Lending
bullets.body: The BIS interim final rule (effective ~Nov 19) closed the China remote-access loophole for advanced NVIDIA chips and added destination-based licensing for Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. Billions in data-center deals have stalled since Nov 16, with Citigroup, Standard Chartered, and Singapore banks conducting sweeping reviews; Bain Capital's Bridge Data Centres $6.6B loan delayed and DayOne Data Centers suspended its US listing. NVIDIA asked server partners (affecting DELL, SMCI) to halt shipments to SE Asia while cloud providers have 90 days to prove end-clients are not restricted entities.

bullets.title: NVIDIA Faces Governance Crisis: S&P Downgrade Watch, Pentagon DPA Threat
bullets.body: S&P placed NVIDIA on downgrade watch citing governance concerns following CEO turmoil, while Pentagon officials reportedly discussed invoking the Defense Production Act to force NVIDIA to reappoint Jensen Huang as CEO on national security grounds. The stock saw SOX fall 8% intraday before closing down 0.65%; aggregate short exposure in AI stocks is at multi-year highs as a percentage of total global gross exposure.

bullets.title: GPU Spot Prices Collapsing; Neoclouds Offloading B300 Systems
bullets.body: SpaceX cut spot GPU rental rates for NVIDIA B200/B300 to $10–12/GPU-hour from $15–15.50 (a 28% reduction), and already-deployed B300 systems are appearing on the secondary market as SE Asia operators reduce exposure. Banks are stopping funding for neoclouds with Chinese customer contracts (ByteDance, Tencent), and GPU sellers are actively seeking new buyers amid the Chinese access clampdown.

bullets.title: Semiconductor Cycle Peak Behind Us; Jefferies Sees Trough H1-28, Rerating Rally H2-27
bullets.body: The semiconductor cycle peaked in June 2026 at 94–135% YoY growth (highest on record), driven by memory pricing, with valuations peaking five months ahead of the underlying cycle. Jefferies expects the earliest trough in H1-28 with a re-rating rally from H2-27; the market is currently selling off pricing in 2027 EPS cuts rather than dragging them to 2028, which paradoxically shortens the downcycle. TSMC and Samsung have halted <16nm shipments to Chinese firms under new US export restrictions.

bullets.title: DRAM Pricing Outlook Softens; 2028 Broad Downturn Risk Flagged
bullets.body: TrendForce cut its 1Q27 DRAM price forecast to +3–8% QoQ from +5–10%, with 2H27 expected flat and LPDDR4X/consumer DRAM down 5–10% in 4Q27. Morgan Stanley's bear case envisions DRAM price declines exceeding 15% QoQ from 1Q28 as bit supply grows 25–30% in 2027–28, though HBM demand remains robust at 80% YoY bit growth in 2027. Citi separately notes global DRAM is undersupplied in 2027 with DRAM revenue projected at $1.15trn (+69% YoY).

bullets.title: Thanksgiving Bounce Boosts Risk Sentiment; Hedge Fund Positioning Reset May Be Mature
bullets.body: US equities saw an intraday Thanksgiving recovery that spilled into APAC and EU, with over 70% of SPX names closing higher. Hedge fund net exposure has fallen >30% from its 12-month high — comparable to late 2018 and March 2020 — suggesting the positioning reset may be well advanced. US semis saw ~3-sigma net selling over 20 days with shorts around +4-sigma, potentially setting the stage for reversal if prices establish a positive trend.

bullets.title: October Core PCE In-Line at +0.3% m/m; Fed/ECB Rate Hike Expectations Pared
bullets.body: October core PCE rose 0.3% m/m, in line with consensus and matching September's pace, providing no upside inflation surprise. Markets have priced out roughly one rate hike each from the Fed and ECB over the past week on easing inflation impulses, while Brent crude is expected to fall to $75–80/bbl, lowering global inflation from 4.4% toward 2–2.5% in 1H27.

bullets.title: US Q3 GDP Revised Sharply Higher to 4.3% Annualized
bullets.body: US Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3% annualized from a prior estimate of 3.4%, with the upside driven by broadening business spending. The revision reinforces the soft-landing narrative and supports the case for continued corporate earnings resilience.

bullets.title: AI Infra Cycle Still Strong Fundamentally, But Investor Sentiment Near Trough
bullets.body: JPM's APAC Tech conference found YTD token consumption up 25x, with Asian supply chains running at full capacity for a 2–3 year AI compute ramp — yet only 2% of investors believe AI hardware stocks are oversold after the recent correction. Three catalysts are needed for sentiment recovery: successful US AI IPOs, clear AI data-center policy, and AI server supply chain revenue reassessment; sentiment could bottom in Q1 2027. The AI infrastructure correction appears disproportionately large and consistent with positioning unwinds rather than fundamental deterioration.

bullets.title: AI Datacenter Power Forecast Raised to 303GW by 2028; Liquid Cooling TAM Surging
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised its 2028 AI datacenter installed power base forecast to 303GW (38% CAGR 2025–28), driven by incremental CoWoS allocations and higher GPU/ASIC shipments. The cooling component TAM was revised up with a ~128% CAGR 2025–28 as all major ASICs adopt double-sided cold plate design in 4Q26/2027; server PSU market expected to grow ~83% to $53bn by 2028. HVDC adoption was lowered to 10–15%/30–35% for VR/VRU cycles due to heat-dissipation constraints and Kyber delay.

bullets.title: AI Valuation Skepticism Deepens: Anthropic Post-IPO Decline, SoftBank Credit Risk at 4-Year High
bullets.body: Anthropic's post-IPO stock decline is intensifying scrutiny on lofty AI company valuations, while SoftBank's credit risk has reached a four-year high amid AI investment concerns and rising funding costs. CoreWeave is seeking a $4.5B chip-backed loan amid rising debt concerns, and an AI-focused hedge fund (Situational Awareness) lost 65% in Q3; Polymarket odds for an OpenAI IPO by mid-2027 have dropped sharply.

bullets.title: BoJ on Track to Hike to 2.25% by Year-End 2027; Japan GDP Forecast 0.9%
bullets.body: JPMorgan forecasts the BoJ will raise rates to 2% through mid-2027 and reach 2.25% by year-end, with real rates remaining negative and limiting near-term economic drag. Japan GDP is forecast at 0.9% for 2027 with domestic demand above potential; core CPI is expected to spike to 3.9% in 1Q27 before moderating to 1.6% by 4Q27 as subsidies roll off. Morgan Stanley separately favors Japan over EM and China on a risk/reward basis for 2027.

bullets.title: JPM Constructive on Asia Equities 2027: MXASJ Base Target 1200, CSI-300 Target 4800
bullets.body: JPMorgan sets MXASJ targets at 1200 base / 1500 bull / 900 bear for end-2027 on US$115 EPS, assuming the AI supercycle resets rather than ends. CSI-300 targets are 4800 base / 5600 bull / 3500 bear; China policy support is expected for the domestic AI supply chain and 'Six Networks' in coming months. Morgan Stanley sees China real GDP at 4.4% in 2027 with reflation expected from 2028 on Industry 5.0 gains.

bullets.title: Hong Kong and Chinese Tech Equities Broadly at 52-Week Lows; Afternoon Bounce +2–3%
bullets.body: Of 146 Asian stocks hitting 52-week extremes on Nov 25–26, 114 were at lows — concentrated in Chinese batteries, semiconductors, autos, and financials — with names like CATL down 44%, BYD down 41%, and Baidu down 47% from their 52-week highs. The Hang Seng recovered mid-morning, with the index up 2.15% and the Tech Index up 3.20%, led by AI/computing stocks up 5–14% on a consolidation bounce, while China ADRs gained 1.87% overnight.

bullets.title: US Chip Curbs Stall Data-Center Lending Globally; Lenders Exiting Chinese-Linked Exposure
bullets.body: Beyond SE Asia, US chip restrictions are disrupting billions in loans tied to ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent globally, with lenders concerned about legal risk. Deals near completion are now in doubt, some lenders are seeking to sell exposure but finding no buyers, and the BlackRock-led consortium is considering lowering its offer for an Asia Pacific data center portfolio.

bullets.title: NVDA B300 Lead Times Stretch to 40 Weeks as AI Supply Crunch Intensifies
bullets.body: Citi reports NVIDIA B300 GPU lead times have stretched to 26–40 weeks versus 14–26 weeks for GB300, with new orders not fulfilling until 2Q27–3Q27. NVIDIA is scaling back GeForce RTX 50 shipments to prioritize AI products; Samsung faces severe HBM base die capacity shortages with wafer requirements projected to double to ~30k 4nm-equivalent wafers/month in 2027.

bullets.title: Disney Wins TRO Halting FCC Review of ABC Broadcast Licenses
bullets.body: Disney secured a temporary restraining order stopping the FCC from continuing its early review of ABC's broadcast-station licenses, removing near-term regulatory overhang. ABC had filed a First Amendment lawsuit in August 2026 claiming FCC investigations were retaliatory.

bullets.title: Black Friday Macro Read: AMZN eComm Concerns on Wealth Effect; META Muse Integrated with Walmart
bullets.body: Goldman flags possible eCommerce concerns for AMZN into Black Friday amid wealth effect questions from the AI stock selloff. Conversely, META's Muse AI shopping agent is now integrated with Walmart for Black Friday deals, with META shares up 3.4% on the news. SemiAnalysis also flagged negative checks on GOOGL ad spending in both Search and YouTube.

bullets.title: Temu Commits to EU Consumer Protection Rules; DSA Breach Could Mean 6% Global Revenue Fine
bullets.body: The EU Commission announced Temu has committed to complying with EU consumer protection rules covering fake discounts, fake reviews, pressure selling, forced gamification, and misleading information. A prior preliminary finding of DSA breach for failing to tackle illegal product sales remains outstanding, with a potential fine of up to 6% of total worldwide annual turnover if confirmed.

bullets.title: Upcoming Earnings Catalyst Cluster: MRVL, CRM, MDB Reporting Early December
bullets.body: Key tech names scheduled to report in early December include MRVL, CRM, and MDB, alongside retail bellwether RH. These prints will be watched for AI infrastructure demand signals (MRVL), software spending trends (CRM, MDB), and consumer health (RH).
